extracted.intended_audience: general readers / researchers seeking a catalog of Netflix original television series
extracted.subtask_description: A structured list of Netflix original scripted and non-scripted television series organized by region/language, with metadata fields (title, genre, premiere/finale dates, seasons/episodes, runtime, language, notes). Useful for cataloging, reference, or research about Netflix programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the television series (e.g., Ever After High, Dark, Kingdom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown as the primary identifier for each row/entry. Titles may include punctuation or subtitles; sometimes additional disambiguation appears in parentheses or as part of the title. Example entries in the list show the title first in each table row.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre
rubrics_metrics.description: The listed genre(s) or subgenres assigned to the series (e.g., Science fiction, Dark fantasy / Crime, Romantic comedy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genres may be single labels or multiple labels separated by slashes or commas (e.g., 'Mecha / Military science fiction', 'Fantasy / comedy drama'). The page groups shows under headings (like 'Kids & family') but each row also specifies genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premiere
rubrics_metrics.description: The series' premiere date on Netflix (formatted as a date, e.g., January 31, 2020; February 6, 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates when the show first became available. Some entries specify only a year or full date. Used for chronological ordering within sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finale
rubrics_metrics.description: The series' finale or latest known date on Netflix (e.g., August 5, 2016; December 7, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ongoing shows this field may be blank or show an updated most recent date. For limited/ended series it shows the final release date. Some entries list future or projected dates when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasons and episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of seasons and total episodes or parts for the series (e.g., '1 season, 6 episodes', '3 seasons, 52 episodes', '6 chapters, 27 episodes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formats vary: 'seasons, episodes', 'parts', 'collections', or 'chapters'. May include special formatting like '2 parts, 26 episodes' or '5 seasons, 17 episodes'. Use as a compact measure of series extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runtime
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical runtime (per episode) expressed as a range in minutes (e.g., '24–33 min', '43–77 min', '9–16 min').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows episode length ranges; some entries show a single minute value or wide ranges (e.g., 45–73 min). For anthology/collections runtime may vary by episode. Useful for classifying by episode length (short-form vs standard vs feature-length).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary language(s) of dialogue for the series (e.g., English, Japanese, No dialogue, Korean, French).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language is listed per entry and sometimes implied by the country/language grouping. Notes may indicate 'No dialogue' or multilingual productions. Useful for grouping by original production language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region / Country grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Section headings that group series by language or national/regional origin (e.g., 'Arabic', 'Danish', 'Japanese', 'Korean', 'Portuguese').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page is organized into subsections by language/region; each subsection contains a table with the same metadata columns. These groupings indicate the production/origin context used by the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes / Annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Free-text notes or annotations attached to entries (e.g., '[a]', 'collections', 'parts', statuses like 'anthology', 'No dialogue', or other editorial footnotes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes field captures special cases: format notes (collections/parts), production remarks, reference markers (superscript letters/numbers), and other contextual remarks (e.g., previously aired elsewhere). Entries often include bracketed citation markers which refer to footnotes on the full page.
